entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
---------
Dusab Birua @ Dusub Birua ... ... Appellant Versus The State of Jharkhand ... ... Respondent

---------
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA ----------

For the Appellant : Mr. Anjani Kumar, Advocate For the Respondent : Mr. Anup Pawan Topno,
A.P.P.
th 06/Dated: 08 August, 2025 I.A. No.10203 of 2025 1.

Heard Mr. Anjani Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Anup Pawan Topno, learned A.P.P for the State.
2.
This application has been preferred on behalf of appellant for grant of bail to the appellant during pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376(2)(l) and under Section 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years along with fine of Rs.10,000/-.
4. It has been alleged that the victim who is the sister-in-law of the informant was subjected to rape by the appellant and other co-convicts.

It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant referring to the evidence of the victim who has been examined as P.W.7 that she used to sleep in Anganwadi Kendra, therefore, it cannot be said with certainty that the appellant was involved in committing rape upon the victim.
Learned counsel submits that other co-convicts have been granted bail by this court and the appellant is in custody since 10.09.2021.

Dusab Birua @ Dusub Birua vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2010943/
1 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Anup Pawan Topno, learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant and submitted that on account of the act of the appellant, the victim was carrying a pregnancy of 24-26 weeks.
6. The evidence of the victim clearly reveals that this appellant as well as the other co-convict had committed rape upon the victim which resulted in her becoming pregnant.
The evidence of P.W. 5 has supported the said facts.
7. On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.
8. Accordingly, 10203 of 2025 stands rejected.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Amar/-
